newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Savage says 1st half profit rise hard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Savage says 1st half profit rise hard.

text.p: Coal and metals miner Savage Resources Ltd said on Monday that its profit performance in the first quarter of the year to June 30, 1997 had been weaker than in the same quarter a year earlier.
Savage also said it would be be difficult to achieve a stronger first half year profit than that recorded in the first half of 1995/96, given forecast commodity prices.
"Overall, the profit performance of the group's operations was not as strong as in the corresponding quarter of the previous year," Savage said in its quarterly report.

"Given forecast commodity prices and the general outlook for the resources sector, the company currently believes it will be difficult to achieve, for the first half of the current year, a result as strong as the first half of the previous year."

Savage said the continued improvement of its coal operations had been offset by lower zinc revenues in Australian dollars, lower germanium and acid contributions and the effects of a roaster shutdown in August.
"The contribution from germanium sales fluctuates from quarter to quarter depending not only on price, but timing of the six monthly shipments and the extent of any forward sales," Savage said.
"The next shipment is scheduled for November 1996 and is estimated to be at least double the size of the previous shipment," it said.

Savage said its zinc unit in the United States produced 23,283 tonnes of saleable zinc in the quarter, down from 26,054 tonnes a year earlier. This was due to the planned shutdown of a roaster at Clarksville.

"This took longer than anticipated and difficulties were experienced in moving the cell house back from a holding pattern to full production," Savage said, adding the shutdown reduced production by about 4,000 tonnes.
"However, since provision for a major periodic roaster shutdown is made in the accounts, the financial effect on the year's result will not be significant," it said.
Savage said coal output from its Liddell project in the Hunter Valley during the quarter exceeded the annual rate of 2.2 million tonnes per annum.
Savage posted a first half profit in 1995/96 of A$11.15 million, up from a A$140,000 profit in the previous corresponding half year.
Savage's share price was down one cent at A$1.26 at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), having earlier risen to A$1.28.
